name: Riyad Bank
legal_name: Riyad Bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: 1957 (Royal Decree and Council of Ministers' Resolution No. 91 dated 23 Nov 1957; CR 1010001054 dated 18 Nov 1957); listed on Tadawul January 1993
ownership_summary: Tadawul-listed bank. The AR 2025 shareholder chart shows the Public Investment Fund 21.8%, GOSI 10.4%, Al Nahla Trading and Contracting Company 8.7%, Assila Investment Company 8.0%, foreign investors 12.4% and others 38.7% (chart date not stated; shown with 31 Dec 2025 share data). Share capital rose from SAR 30bn to SAR 40bn in H1 2026 through bonus shares (S3). Market capitalisation was SAR 79.64bn at 30 Jun 2026 (S6 slide 7) and SAR 81,420m at 31 Dec 2025 (S5).

shareholders.holder: Al Nahla Trading and Contracting Company

government_link: Yes. PIF (21.8%) and GOSI (10.4%) are the two largest shareholders (AR 2025, S5). The AR's related-party table lists PIF as a 'Major Shareholder'.
group_structure: Parent bank with seven 100%-owned subsidiaries (S3 note 1; S5 pp.96-97): Riyad Capital (CMA-licensed investment arm; profiled separately as sa-riyad-capital), Jeel Digital Innovation Company (technology and fintech arm), 1957 Ventures Fund (fintech venture fund), Ithra Al-Riyad Real Estate Company, Esnad Al-Riyadh (HR services), Curzon Street Properties Limited (Isle of Man) and Riyad Financial Markets (Cayman; derivatives). International: London branch, Houston agency, Singapore representative office. Double counting: Riyad Capital's assets, income and AUM are consolidated in the bank's figures and its 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment, which the AR says represents Riyad Capital. Do not add sa-riyad-capital metrics to this record.

footprint: Saudi Arabia: 332 licensed branches at 30 Jun 2026 (S3 note 1); the AR reports 224 operating branches, over 1,670 ATMs and over 168,800 POS terminals at end-2025 (S5 pp.86-87, 14-15). The 2Q26 presentation shows 1,590 ATMs and 153,360 POS (S6 slide 5). Private Banking centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar (S9). International: London branch, Houston agency, Singapore representative office (S3).
customer_segments: Retail: mass, youth (Token), affluent tiers Silver, Golden and Diamond, and Private Banking (HNW); MSME; corporate and multinationals; institutional/treasury clients (S5, S9-S12). Retail customer base 2.69 million at end-2025: affluent +8%, private +14%, mass +7% in 2025 (S5 pp.84-85).
business_lines: Four reportable segments (S3 note 14): Retail banking; Corporate banking (incl. MSME); Treasury and investment; Investment banking and brokerage (Riyad Capital: asset management, brokerage, custody, advisory, investment banking). H1 2026 total operating income of SAR 9,349.9m split Corporate 5,700.0m, Retail 2,084.0m, Treasury 1,072.9m, Investment banking and brokerage 493.0m (about 5%). Private and Affluent Banking sit inside Retail Banking. Other: bancassurance distribution, digital Gold Account, fintech (Jeel, 1957 Ventures). The bank offers Islamic (non-conventional) products under an independent Shariah Board.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Riyad Bank serves wealth clients through Private Banking (three centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar; dedicated full-time RM; positioned as 'Elevate your Wealth Management'), the affluent tiers Diamond, Golden and Silver, and its 100%-owned Riyad Capital (CMA licence 07070-37). Riyad Capital managed SAR 97.5bn at end-2025 and SAR 101.3bn at 30 Jun 2026, and held SAR 1,048bn in custody at end-2025. In 2025 Private Banking AUM grew 5% and interest-bearing deposits 32%; private clients rose 14% and affluent 8%; the Al Khobar PB centre was completed and work on a new Jeddah centre began. The bank app's 'Investments' menu covers time deposits and IPO subscriptions, and a Shariah-compliant digital Gold Account launched in 2025. Equities, funds and international trading run in separate Riyad Capital apps (Riyad Capital, Riyad Global, Riyad Dawli), which need a Riyad Capital investment account. In 2025 Riyad Capital launched Mostashary, an in-house robo-advisory tool in its app. For 2026 the bank plans a new 'Elite' tier within Affluent Banking and a Treasury bond programme extended to Private and Affluent clients. Its 2030 strategy themes are Hyperscale Retail, Wholesale, 'AI to-the-core' and a new core banking system.

asset_management.detail: Through Riyad Capital (100%): AUM SAR 97.5bn at 31 Dec 2025 (incl. SAR 14.0bn non-interest-based funds) and SAR 101.3bn at 2Q26. Public equity, fixed income, multi-asset, money market and REIT funds; private funds; DPM. See sa-riyad-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through Riyad Capital: Saudi, GCC and international markets via the Riyad Capital, Riyad Global and Riyad Dawli apps and online platforms; margin financing. Brokerage value traded SAR 44.7bn in H1 2026, down 30% YoY from SAR 63.5bn (S6 slide 41).

digital_investing.detail: Bank app (Riyad Mobile, fully redesigned with 125+ new features in 2025): 'Investments' menu lists 'Book Time Deposit' and 'IPO' (S13). Shariah-compliant Gold Account to buy, sell and hold gold digitally, launched 2025 (S5 pp.92-93). Trading, funds and the Mostashary robo-adviser sit in separate Riyad Capital apps that use Riyad Online credentials and need a Riyad Capital investment account (S24). No in-app funds, model portfolios or international investing found in the bank app itself.

advisory.detail: Private Banking cites 'enriched advisory capabilities' (S5). Diamond Banking offers a financial consulting service when opening an investment account (S10). Riyad Capital runs investment advisory for individuals and institutions (see sa-riyad-capital).

discretionary.detail: Riyad Capital offers Discretionary Portfolio Management under an Investment Management Agreement (see sa-riyad-capital).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Riyad Capital launched 'Mostashary', an in-house robo-advisory tool in the Riyad Capital app offering automated investment portfolios, goal-based planning and risk profiling; SAR 1.7m invested in its first month (2025). Not in the bank app.

funds_platform.detail: Riyad Capital distributes its own public funds and, per its advisory page, CMA-registered funds 'managed in-house and by third-party providers' (see sa-riyad-capital). No fund-platform vendor named.

structured_products.detail: Offered by Riyad Capital's advisory service ('tailor made structured products'; see sa-riyad-capital). Not mentioned on the bank's Private Banking page. Treasury plans to extend coverage to Private and Affluent clients in 2026 (S5 pp.94-95).

private_markets.detail: Riyad Capital private and real-estate funds (Riyad Taqnia Fund; real estate portfolio SAR 10bn; up to SAR 6bn Makkah transit-oriented fund with Saudi Railway Company); lead investor in a USD 250m pre-IPO round in 2025 (S5 pp.96-99). The bank also owns 1957 Ventures Fund (fintech VC).

islamic_wealth.detail: Non-conventional (Islamic) products under an independent Shariah Board; Islamic time deposits SAR 66.8bn at 30 Jun 2026 (S3); Shariah-compliant Gold Account (S5); Riyad Capital non-interest-based funds SAR 14.0bn at end-2025 (S4 note 42).

partners.what: Moved from design and UX/UI provider to a 'fully integrated delivery partner embedded directly into Jeel's operations' (product management, delivery governance, journey design)
Cloud-native composable banking for the Jeel Sandbox, hosted on Google Cloud Platform; initial fintech pilot cohort expected late 2025
MoU with Jeel: proofs-of-concept in the Jeel Sandbox on cross-border payment corridors, digital-asset custody and tokenisation
MoU with Jeel to bring AI capabilities to market
Jeel supports fintech licensing and regulatory testing with SAMA and Fintech Saudi via the Jeel Sandbox

Related-party contracts: 'Brokerage Services Contract - Mubasher Pro Direct Trading Program' (SAR 828,000, expiry 31 Dec 2025) and 'Mubasher Brokerage Services Systems and integration of existing trading services' (SAR 57,500)

initiatives.what: Nadir Al-Koraya became CEO, succeeding Tareq Al-Sadhan

Launched a Shariah-compliant digital Gold Account (buy, sell, hold gold in digital channels); redesigned Riyad Mobile app with 125+ features, in-app personal finance management tool, Samsung Pay and Google Pay
Riyad Capital launched the in-house Mostashary robo-advisory tool (SAR 1.7m invested in first month) and the Wa'i Mali youth financial-literacy series

Jeel became the bank's main development partner (Riyad Mobile, MSME platform, Home Buying Ecosystem) and won its first external client; Center of Intelligence launched the first enterprise AI strategy and moved GenAI pilots into production
Jeel and Mambu partnership for the Jeel fintech sandbox (developed with Fintech Saudi; hosted on Google Cloud)
Jeel signed an MoU with Ripple for sandbox proofs-of-concept on payments, digital-asset custody and tokenisation
Stated 2026 plans: new 'Elite' tier within Affluent Banking; Treasury bond programme and coverage of Private and Affluent clients; Agentic AI pilots; embedded finance; Open Finance payment initiation

2030 strategy: four themes - Hyperscale Retail (digital acquisition, embedding in third-party ecosystems, loyalty), Wholesale, 'AI to-the-core' (advanced analytics, GenAI, Agentic AI), and a robust core technology foundation with a new core banking system

opportunities: The bank app's investment menu lists only 'Book Time Deposit' and 'IPO' (S13); equities, funds and international investing sit in separate Riyad Capital apps that need a separate investment account (S24)
2026 plans: a new 'Elite' tier within Affluent Banking (S5 pp.88-89) and a Treasury bond programme extended to Private and Affluent clients (S5 pp.94-95)
Wealth segments are growing: in 2025 private clients +14%, affluent +8%, Private Banking AUM +5% and interest-bearing deposits +32% (S5 pp.84-87)
2030 theme 'AI to-the-core' covers 'advanced analytics, GenAI, Agentic AI across the bank including front, middle and back-office' (S6 slide 11); Agentic AI pilots are planned for 2026 (S5 pp.68-69)
Jeel runs a sandbox used for partner proofs-of-concept (Mambu, Oct 2025; Ripple MoU on tokenisation and digital-asset custody, Jan 2026) (S18, S19)
Riyad Capital brokerage value traded fell 30% YoY in H1 2026 (SAR 63.5bn to 44.7bn) and the segment's pre-zakat income fell 12% (S6 slide 41)
barriers: Builds in-house: Jeel is the bank's 'most trusted development partner' with Efigence embedded in its delivery (S5 pp.66-67); Riyad Capital developed its Mostashary robo-adviser in-house (S5 pp.98-99)
Investment licences sit with Riyad Capital (CMA licence 07070-37), so a wealth-product contract would likely be with the subsidiary (S3 note 1; sa-riyad-capital)
Riyad Capital already offers international stocks, ETFs, options and bonds through its Riyad Global app (see sa-riyad-capital)
Islamic products need approval by the bank's Shariah Board (S3 note 1)
incumbent_vendors: Efigence: digital delivery, product management and UX partner embedded in Jeel (S5)
Mambu: core banking for the Jeel Sandbox, hosted on Google Cloud Platform (S18)
Mubasher Financial Network: 'Mubasher Pro Direct Trading Program' brokerage services and brokerage-systems integration contracts (S5)
Interactive Brokers group (inferred): the Riyad Global app's App Store copyright is 'IB Exchange Corp.' (see sa-riyad-capital)
Genesys (social-media contact centre) and Verint (quality assurance) in the contact centre (S5)
